item.title: “So too, Māgandiya, contact with sensual pleasures in the past was painful, very hot, very feverish; contact with sensual pleasures in the future will be…
item.description:
“So too, Māgandiya, contact with sensual pleasures in the past was painful, very hot, very feverish; contact with sensual pleasures in the future will be painful, very hot, very feverish; contact with sensual pleasures in the present is painful, very hot, very feverish. And these beings who have not abandoned lust for sensual pleasures, being consumed by craving for sensual pleasures, burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, with corrupt faculties, perceive as pleasure that which is actually painful contact with sensual pleasures.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 75 – Māgandiyasutta

item.title: “If there is form, Rādha, then there is death, or a killer, or being killed. Therefore, Rādha, you should see form as death, see it…
item.description:
“If there is form, Rādha, then there is death, or a killer, or being killed. Therefore, Rādha, you should see form as death, see it as a killer, see it as being killed, see it as a disease, see it as a boil, see it as a dart, see it as misery, see it as its own misery. One who sees form thus sees rightly.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 23.1

item.title: Behold this adorned appearance, With jewels and earrings, A skeleton covered by skin, Made beautiful by clothes.
item.description:
Behold this adorned appearance,
With jewels and earrings,
A skeleton covered by skin,
Made beautiful by clothes.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 82 – Raṭṭhapālasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “What do you think, Māgandiya? Here, a person formerly was infatuated with forms cognizable by the eye that were desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with…
item.description:
“What do you think, Māgandiya? Here, a person formerly was infatuated with forms cognizable by the eye that were desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. After some time, having known as they actually are the origination, the passing away, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in the case of forms, he abandons craving for forms, removes the fever for forms, and dwells with craving cut off, with mind inwardly peaceful.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 75 – Māgandiyasutta

item.title: “Monks, there are these three kinds of craving. What three? Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence. These, monks, are the three…
item.description:
“Monks, there are these three kinds of craving. What three? Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence. These, monks, are the three kinds of craving.

Bound by the bondage of craving,
Their minds attached to becoming and non-becoming,
Bound by Māra’s bondage,
Those beings are not secure from bondage.
They go on in the wandering,
Gone to birth and death.

But those who have abandoned craving,
Free from craving for becoming and non-becoming,
Having reached the far shore,
In this very world, they have attained
The destruction of the defilements.”

From: Itivuttaka 58

item.title: The Blessed One: “Seeing craving, aversion, and lust, There is no desire for sexual intercourse. What is this, so full of urine and feces? I…
item.description:
The Blessed One:
“Seeing craving, aversion, and lust,
There is no desire for sexual intercourse.
What is this, so full of urine and feces?
I would not wish even to touch it with my foot.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 4.9
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “For the most part, monks, beings find pleasure in sensual pleasures. But a clansman who has set aside the sickle and the carrying-pole, gone forth…
item.description:
“For the most part, monks, beings find pleasure in sensual pleasures. But a clansman who has set aside the sickle and the carrying-pole, gone forth from the household life into homelessness, is justifiably called ‘a clansman who has gone forth out of faith.’ Why is that? Sensual pleasures are found with youth, these sensual pleasures or others. And, monks, low sensual pleasures, middling sensual pleasures, and supreme sensual pleasures — all are classed as sensual pleasures.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.7
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, sensual pleasures are impermanent, empty, false, of a delusive nature. Monks, this is the mere greeting of a fool built upon deception. Sensual pleasures…
item.description:
“Monks, sensual pleasures are impermanent, empty, false, of a delusive nature. Monks, this is the mere greeting of a fool built upon deception. Sensual pleasures present and future, perceptions of sensual pleasure present and future — both belong to Māra’s realm, Māra’s domain, Māra’s bait, Māra’s food.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 106 – Āneñjasappāyasutta

item.title: “Good sirs, what is suffering? Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, sickness is suffering, death is suffering, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, despair are suffering, not…
item.description:
“Good sirs, what is suffering? Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, sickness is suffering, death is suffering, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, despair are suffering, not getting what one wants is suffering; in short, the five clinging-aggregates are suffering. This, good sirs, is called suffering. Good sirs, what is the origin of suffering? It is craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, delighting here and there; that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence. This, good sirs, is called the origin of suffering.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 9 – Sammādiṭṭhisutta

item.title: “Venerable Gotama, I have a perplexity and doubt: ‘How should one understand the Dhamma of the ascetic Gotama?’” - “Vaccha, your perplexity is enough, your…
item.description:
“Venerable Gotama, I have a perplexity and doubt: ‘How should one understand the Dhamma of the ascetic Gotama?’” - “Vaccha, your perplexity is enough, your doubt is enough. It is on this point that perplexity and doubt have arisen. I declare the rebirth of one who has clinging, Vaccha, not of one who has no clinging. Just as, Vaccha, a fire burns when there is fuel, not when there is no fuel. So too, Vaccha, I declare rebirth for one who has clinging, not for one who has no clinging.” - “Venerable Gotama, when the wind blows a fire far away, what does Venerable Gotama declare as the fuel for that fire?” - “Vaccha, when the wind blows a fire far away, I say that the wind is its fuel. At that time, Vaccha, the wind is the fuel (upādāna).” - “Venerable Gotama, when a being gives up this body and is reborn in another body, what does Venerable Gotama declare as the fuel for that being?” - “Vaccha, when a being gives up this body and is reborn in another body, I declare that at that time craving (taṇhā) is the fuel (upādāna).”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 44.9
